description: 'Iron Goddess of Mercy'. A legendary oolong from Anxi, China, celebrated for its complex floral aroma and lingering sweet aftertaste, known as 'Guan Yin Yun'. Its robust leaves can withstand intricate processing, yielding two distinct styles: a modern, vibrantly floral green style and a traditional, deeply roasted style with notes of fruit and caramel.

processing_suitability_details: The cultivar's thick, durable leaves are its greatest asset, able to withstand the repeated bruising, shaking, and rolling required to develop its complex aromatics without breaking. This makes it ideal for both light and heavy processing.
oxidation_details: For the modern green style, oxidation is kept low (15-25%). For the traditional baked style, oxidation is higher (30-50%), which develops a fruity base that can stand up to the heavy roasting.
roasting_details: The green style is unroasted or given a very light drying bake. The traditional style is defined by its 'hong bei' (烘焙) charcoal roasting, which can take place over many hours at low temperatures to build deep, complex flavors.
style_versatility: Highly versatile within the oolong category. Its two primary styles are worlds apart. It can also be processed into a unique, floral black tea, though this is less common.

description: 'Original Mountain'. A close genetic relative of Tie Guan Yin from the neighboring mountains of Anxi. Ben Shan is known for producing a lighter-bodied oolong with a very clear, high-pitched floral aroma, often described as being more straightforward and less complex than its famous cousin. It is a popular and more affordable daily-drinker oolong.
parentage: Close genetic relative of Tie Guan Yin, selected from the same Anxi heirloom population.
plant_type: Upright bush type, similar in appearance to Tie Guan Yin but slightly less robust (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in similar conditions to Tie Guan Yin but is often found in slightly different microclimates within the greater Anxi region.

processing_suitability_details: Ben Shan's leaves are thinner and more delicate than Tie Guan Yin's, making them best suited for light-handed processing. They develop their floral aroma quickly but cannot withstand heavy oxidation or roasting.
oxidation_details: Oxidation is kept very low (10-20%) to preserve its fresh, delicate, and high-pitched floral notes. The goal is to maximize the upfront aroma.
roasting_details: Almost never roasted, other than a final, low-temperature drying bake. Its delicate character would be completely overwhelmed by any significant roasting.
style_versatility: Not very versatile. It excels at one thing: being a light, fresh, and aromatic green-style oolong. It lacks the substance for traditional processing or for making other tea types.

description: 'Hairy Crab'. An Anxi oolong cultivar named for the fine, downy hairs on its fresh leaves and the slightly curled shape of the brewed leaf, thought to resemble a crab. It is known for its forward, fruity-floral aroma, high yield, and early budding, making it a commercially important variety in Anxi.

description: 'Big Red Robe'. The most legendary and revered of all Wuyi Rock Oolongs. While the name refers to a few specific mother trees, most Da Hong Pao on the market is a masterful blend of other high-quality Wuyi cultivars (like Rou Gui and Shui Xian) made in the DHP style. It is the benchmark for the complex 'rock rhyme' (Yan Yun)—a unique mineral taste and texture derived from its rocky terroir.
parentage: The original cultivar is believed to be Qi Dan, which was selected from the native Wuyi heirloom population.
plant_type: Sturdy, medium-sized bush, adapted to rocky terrain (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in the rocky, mineral-rich, and heavily eroded soil of the Wuyi Mountains' core 'Zhengyan' production area. The misty, humid microclimate is crucial.

processing_suitability_details: The leaves of the cultivars used for Da Hong Pao are robust enough to handle the stress of multiple, slow charcoal roasts. The processing goal is to bake the flavor deep into the leaf, creating a tea that unfolds over many infusions.
oxidation_details: Da Hong Pao undergoes significant oxidation (40-60%) to build a rich, fruity, and complex foundation that can support the intensity of the charcoal roasting.
roasting_details: Roasting is the defining step. It involves multiple, long sessions of baking over charcoal embers at controlled temperatures. This process, known as 'hong bei', creates the tea's deep, roasted flavor and smooths out any astringency.
style_versatility: Extremely specialized. The Da Hong Pao name and its associated cultivars are exclusively used for producing this singular, iconic style of Wuyi Rock Oolong. Its entire identity is tied to this specific processing method.

description: 'Cassia' or 'Cinnamon'. Originally a supporting actor in the Wuyi Mountains, Rou Gui has become a superstar in its own right, now one of the most popular and planted Yancha cultivars. It is celebrated for its distinctive and captivating spicy-sweet aroma of cinnamon and ginger, which is layered over the classic Wuyi mineral-rich base.

plant_type: Vigorous, medium-sized, upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Thrives in the rocky terroir of the Wuyi Mountains, which gives it the foundational 'rock rhyme' upon which its signature spice notes are built.

processing_suitability_details: Rou Gui's inherent aromatic compounds are less volatile than those of green oolongs. The challenge of processing is to fully express this spicy character through careful oxidation and a roast that complements, rather than smothers, the aroma.
oxidation_details: Undergoes heavy oxidation (40-60%), similar to other top-tier Yancha, to develop a robust flavor base that harmonizes with its spicy notes.
roasting_details: The charcoal roast is critical. A skilled tea master will apply a roast that is strong enough to create the classic Yancha depth but precise enough to elevate and fix the cinnamon-like fragrance, making it persistent across many infusions.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. Like Da Hong Pao, Rou Gui is almost exclusively processed as a Wuyi Rock Oolong. Its fame and value are entirely dependent on this specific style.
